source_note: Claude Code best practices: compact at a natural break, such as between research and implementation. Both sides run the task in three or two calls of one resumed session. Call 1: the task prompt plus 'Step 1 only: investigate the code and reply with your plan. Do not edit files yet.' With: call 2 is the built-in /compact sent headless to the resumed session (slash commands are enabled for that call only: with --disable-slash-commands Claude Code answers '/compact isn't available in this environment' and compacts nothing), then call 3 'Now implement your plan and finish the task.' Without: call 3 straight after call 1. Slash commands stay off on every task call on both sides, as on days 1-30. Every compaction is recorded (extra: compacts, tokens before and after). Time, cost, turns and tokens are summed over every call, the compact included; the 20-minute cap covers all calls. t1, t2, t3, h2 on Haiku 4.5, 3 runs per task per side.
